issue: applies_to replaces the session path with main_checkout(project) instead of adding it, so a record whose projectPath is the worktree itself no longer matches Scenario: git worktree add ../wt; project-scoped install recorded from a session in wt (projectPath=<wt>); applies_to({projectPath: wt}, wt) is False at ae339e4 and True on origin/dev. toolchain_version reports 'installed only for other projects' and drive.md's gate stops. A stale worktree whose gitdir names a deleted main (maps to /nowhere) regresses the same way. Fix: match if root contains here OR main_checkout(here), plus a fixture with the record at the worktree path

the case-only fixture is skipped on case-sensitive volumes (CI's Linux runner), and no mutation covers it, so the gate cannot fail in CI Scenario: with the samefile branch disabled (return False and ...) macOS reports 46/1 but Linux CI stays green. Fix: monkeypatch os.path.samefile or drive it with an injected predicate so the check runs everywhere, then add the mutation

when skill_version_tag exits 2 (repo unreadable), the block prints 'no release carries that rails-stack version: search origin/dev', which is the wrong advice Scenario: run the block outside a repo: rc=2, stderr 'not a git repository' followed by 'no release carries that version: search origin/dev'. Fix: capture the script's rc and branch on 1 vs 2

the prose says to search each tag the warning names, but the block searches only $ref and fails with 2 when the skill exists only in a later tag of the same version Scenario: a skill added at v1.76.0 under rails-stack 1.42.2: the block exits 2 ('fix the skill name') although a later tag of that version has it. Fix: loop over the named tags in the block

the warning lists every tag that differs from the first, including tags that are identical to each other, which triples the searches for 1.42.2 Scenario: 1.42.2 warns about v1.76.0 v1.77.0 v1.79.0, which share one skills tree (13dad6f4), so there are 2 distinct trees and 4 searches. Fix: name one tag per distinct tree

'the same rule as design-flow's #1421 resolver' cites code that is not on dev (PR #1473 is OPEN), and that PR's worktree mapping has the same shape as B1 Scenario: if #1473 changes or never merges, the bullet cites a rule that does not exist; if it merges unchanged, design-flow inherits B1. Fix: apply the B1 fix to both, or reword the bullet

a worktree of a submodule (gitdir <super>/.git/modules/<m>/worktrees/<w>) maps to the modules gitdir, not to a checkout Scenario: a session in a linked worktree of a submodule compares the record against <super>/.git/modules/<m>, which never matches a projectPath. This is an edge case: document it or skip it deliberately
